citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix an integer $N\ge2$. Write $\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C)$ for the complex $N\times N$ matrices, $U^*=\overline U^{\mathsf T}$ for conjugate transpose, and $I_N$ for the identity matrix. Define the special unitary matrix group

$$SU(N):=\{U\in\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_N,\ \det U=1\},$$

with matrix multiplication and the following real embedded smooth structure. Identify $\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C)$ with $\mathbb R^{2N^2}$ by the real and imaginary matrix entries, and let $\operatorname{Herm}_N=\{H:H^*=H\}$ have its induced real vector-space structure. Equip $U(N)=\{U:U^*U=I_N\}$ with the embedded regular-level-set structure at $I_N$ of the smooth map $F:\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)\to\operatorname{Herm}_N$, $F(U)=U^*U$, where $\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)=\{U:\det U\ne0\}$. Equip $S^1=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with its embedded circle structure and $SU(N)$ with the embedded regular-level-set structure at $1$ of $\det:U(N)\to S^1$. These are the embedded structures in the stated real matrix space. Its real Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(N):=\{X\in\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\ \operatorname{tr}X=0\}$ with bracket $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. The standard unitary representation is the map $\rho:SU(N)\to U(\mathbb C^N,h)$ defined by $\rho(U)v=Uv$, where $h(v,w)=\sum_{j=1}^N\overline{v_j}w_j$ and $U(\mathbb C^N,h)$ consists of the complex-linear maps preserving $h$. Conjugation is $\operatorname{Ad}_U z=UzU^{-1}$ for either $z\in SU(N)$ or $z\in\mathfrak{su}(N)$.

Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the representation $\rho$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas of local sections $(U_\alpha,s_\alpha)$ whose coordinate images are bounded balls, and a subordinate partition of unity with each cutoff compactly supported in its chart. On an overlap write $s_\beta=s_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}$ for its smooth transition map $g_{\alpha\beta}:U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\to SU(N)$. Local representatives of an adjoint section $\xi$ and an adjoint group section $u$ are defined by $\xi(x)=[s_\alpha(x),\xi_\alpha(x)]$ and $u(x)=[s_\alpha(x),u_\alpha(x)]$. They obey the transition rules $\xi_\beta=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}}\xi_\alpha$ and $u_\beta=g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}u_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}$.

For each integer $k>d/2+1$, define $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ by completion of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms, using weak derivatives of their local coefficients. Define $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ as the corresponding completion of smooth group-bundle sections, represented locally by matrix-valued $H^{k+1}$ maps satisfying the stated transition rule. After localization by the partition of unity and extension by zero to the coordinate balls, the higher-order Sobolev embedding gives unique continuous representatives (indeed $C^1$); the group-valued representatives take values in the closed subgroup $SU(N)$ everywhere. This embedding is the point-evaluation convention used below. If $p\in P$ lies over $x$ and $p=s_\alpha(x)h$, define $u(p):=h^{-1}u_\alpha(x)h$. The transition rule makes this independent of the chosen local section, and $u(x)=[p,u(p)]$. In particular, if $p_m=s_\alpha(x_m)h_{\alpha m}$, then $u(p_m)=h_{\alpha m}^{-1}u_\alpha(x_m)h_{\alpha m}$ is the value in the $p_m$-trivialization. The map $\widetilde u:P\to P$ defined by $\widetilde u(p):=p\,u(p)$ is a $C^1$ bundle automorphism over $\operatorname{id}_M$, with inverse $\widetilde{u^{-1}}$; it is smooth when $u$ is smooth. Conversely, if $\Phi:P\to P$ is a $C^1$ bundle automorphism over $\operatorname{id}_M$ commuting with the right $SU(N)$ action, write $\Phi(p)=p\,g_p$ for the unique $g_p\in SU(N)$. Equivariance gives $g_{ph}=h^{-1}g_ph$, so $u(x):=[p,g_p]$ for $p\in P_x$ is a well-defined $C^1$ adjoint-group section. These assignments are inverse; in the smooth case they identify smooth sections with the smooth gauge group defined by principal-bundle automorphisms.

Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$, equivalently the sections whose associated bundle automorphism fixes $p_m$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology and multiplication $[u][v]=[uv]$, well-defined since $Z_N$ is central.

Specify its Hilbert Lie structure as follows, using the Hilbert Lie structure on $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ established by the calculus lemma. Let $q:\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ be the coset projection. Since $Z_N$ is finite and the group is Hausdorff, choose an identity chart neighborhood $V$ with $V^{-1}V\cap Z_N=\{e\}$, by continuity of $(v,w)\mapsto v^{-1}w$ at $(e,e)$. The map $q$ is open because $q^{-1}(q(O))=\bigcup_{z\in Z_N}Oz$ for every open $O$. Consequently $q|_{uV}:uV\to q(uV)$ is a homeomorphism for each $u$, and transport the translated Hilbert charts through these maps. On an overlap, two lifts differ locally by multiplication by a fixed element of the discrete group $Z_N$, so chart changes are smooth. Distinct cosets have disjoint open neighborhoods: if $v^{-1}w\notin Z_N$, continuity and finiteness give neighborhoods $O_v,O_w$ with $O_v^{-1}O_w\cap Z_N=\varnothing$, and their images under $q$ are disjoint. Thus the quotient is Hausdorff. Its countable base descends from that of the Sobolev section space by the open map $q$. Multiplication and inversion are smooth in these charts because they lift locally to the corresponding smooth operations on $\mathcal G_{k+1}$. This defines a Hilbert Lie group with the stated quotient topology, and $q$ is a local diffeomorphism.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty:=\Gamma^\infty(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ be the group of smooth adjoint-group sections under pointwise multiplication, identified above with the smooth gauge group. Give it the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. For a connection form $\omega$, write $A_\alpha=s_\alpha^*\omega$ for its local form. The right-principal convention gives $A_\beta=g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}A_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}+g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}dg_{\alpha\beta}$. The right gauge action is locally $A_\alpha^u:=u_\alpha^{-1}A_\alpha u_\alpha+u_\alpha^{-1}du_\alpha$. For smooth $u$, this is the pullback by $\widetilde u$: for $X\in T_xM$, $d(\widetilde u\circ s_\alpha)_xX=d(R_{u_\alpha(x)})_{s_\alpha(x)}\,ds_\alpha(X)+(u_\alpha^{-1}du_\alpha(X))_P(s_\alpha(x)u_\alpha(x))$, and the connection equivariance and vertical reproduction identities give the displayed formula. For Sobolev $u$, the calculus lemma verifies that the local forms patch under the stated transition rules and define a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the configuration data of the preceding definition. For every integer $k>d/2+1$, all finite-atlas Sobolev norms on the specified section and form spaces are equivalent, and $H^k$ embeds continuously in $C^1$. Put $\mathcal M:=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C)$, where $SU(N)$ acts by matrix conjugation and $H^r(\mathcal M)$ uses the same finite-atlas completion for each integer $r\ge0$. Pointwise multiplication is a bounded bilinear map $H^k(\mathcal M)\times H^k(\mathcal M)\to H^k(\mathcal M)$; its restriction to adjoint Lie algebra sections has this matrix-bundle target, whereas the commutator is a bounded bilinear map $H^k(\operatorname{ad}P)\times H^k(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^k(\operatorname{ad}P)$. The set $\mathcal G_{k+1}=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ is a Hilbert Lie group modeled on $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$, and the right gauge action $\mathcal A_k\times\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\mathcal A_k$ is smooth. At $(A,e)$ its differential, in the affine and exponential coordinates, is

$$D\bigl((A+a)^{\exp\xi}\bigr)_{(0,0)}(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi,$$

where $a\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the first definition, and let $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$. Define the covariant Laplacian on adjoint sections by

$$\Delta_A:=d_A^*d_A:H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\longrightarrow H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P).$$

Then $\Delta_A$ is a bounded isomorphism with bounded inverse $G_A:H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$. Moreover,

$$H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)=\operatorname{im}d_A\oplus\ker d_A^*,$$

and the bounded projection onto $\operatorname{im}d_A$ is $\Pi_A=d_AG_Ad_A^*$. In operator-norm neighborhoods of each irreducible $A$, the inverse $G_A$ and projection $\Pi_A$ depend smoothly on $A$. The imported smooth-coefficient Green theorem is used only for a smooth reference connection; the asserted operator $\Delta_A$ itself may have Sobolev coefficients.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be real
Banach spaces, let $U \subseteq X \times Y$ be open for the product metric, let
$F : U \to Z$ be of class $C^k$ with $k \ge 1$
([[def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces]]), and let $(a,b) \in U$ with
$F(a,b) = 0$. Let $D_XF(a,b) := DF(a,b)\circ i_X$ and
$D_YF(a,b) := DF(a,b)\circ i_Y$ be the partial derivatives, where
$i_X(x) := (x,0)$ and $i_Y(y) := (0,y)$. If $D_YF(a,b) : Y \to Z$ is a bounded
linear isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $A \subseteq X$ of $a$
and $B \subseteq Y$ of $b$ and a unique map $g : A \to B$ of class $C^k$ such
that

$$\{\,(x,y) \in A \times B : F(x,y) = 0\,\} = \{\,(x,g(x)) : x \in A\,\},$$

and along the graph $Dg$ satisfies
$$Dg(x) = -\,D_YF\bigl(x,g(x)\bigr)^{-1}\,D_XF\bigl(x,g(x)\bigr) \qquad (x \in A).$$
In particular $g(a) = b$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$, $Y$ be real
Banach spaces, let $U \subseteq X$ be open, let $f : U \to Y$ be of class $C^k$
with $k \ge 1$ ([[def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces]]), and let $a \in U$. If
$Df(a) : X \to Y$ is a bounded linear isomorphism — that is, $Df(a)$ is
bijective and its inverse $Df(a)^{-1} : Y \to X$ is bounded — then there are
open sets $U_0 \subseteq U$ with $a \in U_0$ and $V_0 \subseteq Y$ with
$f(a) \in V_0$ such that $f|_{U_0} : U_0 \to V_0$ is a bijection and its inverse
$g := (f|_{U_0})^{-1} : V_0 \to U_0$ is of class $C^k$, with

$$Dg\bigl(f(x)\bigr) = Df(x)^{-1} \qquad \text{for every } x \in U_0 .$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces over the same scalar field
([[def-banach-space]]).

1. If $R\in\mathcal B(X)$ satisfies $\|R\|<1$
   ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), then $I-R$ is
   invertible with inverse the operator-norm limit of the partial sums
   $\sum_{n<N}R^n$, the norm limit being taken in
   $\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]), and
   $$\Bigl\|\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}R^n\Bigr\|\le\frac{1}{1-\|R\|}.$$
2. If $A\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ is invertible with $A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$ and
   $E\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ satisfies $\|A^{-1}E\|<1$, then $A+E$ is invertible
   with $(A+E)^{-1}=\bigl(I+A^{-1}E\bigr)^{-1}A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth-coefficient second-order differential operator on $E$, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)I_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors. Thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$; the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$ with $kp>n$. Then there is $C(n,p,k,\Omega)$ with
$$\|uv\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\qquad(u,v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega)),$$
so $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is a Banach algebra; the constants and the conclusion may depend on the choice of equivalent Sobolev norm only through $C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

derivations.claim: The finite center $Z_N$ acts freely on the Banach Lie group $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ by translations. Around any group element choose an open chart whose distinct $Z_N$-translates are disjoint; the quotient map restricts to a chart on each such neighborhood, with transition maps given by smooth translations. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix an integer $N\ge2$. Write $\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C)$ for the complex $N\times N$ matrices, $U^*=\overline U^{\mathsf T}$ for conjugate transpose, and $I_N$ for the identity matrix. Define the special unitary matrix group

$$SU(N):=\{U\in\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_N,\ \det U=1\},$$

with matrix multiplication and the following real embedded smooth structure. Identify $\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C)$ with $\mathbb R^{2N^2}$ by the real and imaginary matrix entries, and let $\operatorname{Herm}_N=\{H:H^*=H\}$ have its induced real vector-space structure. Equip $U(N)=\{U:U^*U=I_N\}$ with the embedded regular-level-set structure at $I_N$ of the smooth map $F:\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)\to\operatorname{Herm}_N$, $F(U)=U^*U$, where $\operatorname{GL}_N(\mathbb C)=\{U:\det U\ne0\}$. Equip $S^1=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with its embedded circle structure and $SU(N)$ with the embedded regular-level-set structure at $1$ of $\det:U(N)\to S^1$. These are the embedded structures in the stated real matrix space. Its real Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(N):=\{X\in\operatorname{Mat}_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\ \operatorname{tr}X=0\}$ with bracket $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. The standard unitary representation is the map $\rho:SU(N)\to U(\mathbb C^N,h)$ defined by $\rho(U)v=Uv$, where $h(v,w)=\sum_{j=1}^N\overline{v_j}w_j$ and $U(\mathbb C^N,h)$ consists of the complex-linear maps preserving $h$. Conjugation is $\operatorname{Ad}_U z=UzU^{-1}$ for either $z\in SU(N)$ or $z\in\mathfrak{su}(N)$.

Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the representation $\rho$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas of local sections $(U_\alpha,s_\alpha)$ whose coordinate images are bounded balls, and a subordinate partition of unity with each cutoff compactly supported in its chart. On an overlap write $s_\beta=s_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}$ for its smooth transition map $g_{\alpha\beta}:U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\to SU(N)$. Local representatives of an adjoint section $\xi$ and an adjoint group section $u$ are defined by $\xi(x)=[s_\alpha(x),\xi_\alpha(x)]$ and $u(x)=[s_\alpha(x),u_\alpha(x)]$. They obey the transition rules $\xi_\beta=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}}\xi_\alpha$ and $u_\beta=g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}u_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}$.

For each integer $k>d/2+1$, define $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ by completion of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms, using weak derivatives of their local coefficients. Define $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ as the corresponding completion of smooth group-bundle sections, represented locally by matrix-valued $H^{k+1}$ maps satisfying the stated transition rule. After localization by the partition of unity and extension by zero to the coordinate balls, the higher-order Sobolev embedding gives unique continuous representatives (indeed $C^1$); the group-valued representatives take values in the closed subgroup $SU(N)$ everywhere. This embedding is the point-evaluation convention used below. If $p\in P$ lies over $x$ and $p=s_\alpha(x)h$, define $u(p):=h^{-1}u_\alpha(x)h$. The transition rule makes this independent of the chosen local section, and $u(x)=[p,u(p)]$. In particular, if $p_m=s_\alpha(x_m)h_{\alpha m}$, then $u(p_m)=h_{\alpha m}^{-1}u_\alpha(x_m)h_{\alpha m}$ is the value in the $p_m$-trivialization. The map $\widetilde u:P\to P$ defined by $\widetilde u(p):=p\,u(p)$ is a $C^1$ bundle automorphism over $\operatorname{id}_M$, with inverse $\widetilde{u^{-1}}$; it is smooth when $u$ is smooth. Conversely, if $\Phi:P\to P$ is a $C^1$ bundle automorphism over $\operatorname{id}_M$ commuting with the right $SU(N)$ action, write $\Phi(p)=p\,g_p$ for the unique $g_p\in SU(N)$. Equivariance gives $g_{ph}=h^{-1}g_ph$, so $u(x):=[p,g_p]$ for $p\in P_x$ is a well-defined $C^1$ adjoint-group section. These assignments are inverse; in the smooth case they identify smooth sections with the smooth gauge group defined by principal-bundle automorphisms.

Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$, equivalently the sections whose associated bundle automorphism fixes $p_m$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology and multiplication $[u][v]=[uv]$, well-defined since $Z_N$ is central.

Specify its Hilbert Lie structure as follows, using the Hilbert Lie structure on $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ established by the calculus lemma. Let $q:\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ be the coset projection. Since $Z_N$ is finite and the group is Hausdorff, choose an identity chart neighborhood $V$ with $V^{-1}V\cap Z_N=\{e\}$, by continuity of $(v,w)\mapsto v^{-1}w$ at $(e,e)$. The map $q$ is open because $q^{-1}(q(O))=\bigcup_{z\in Z_N}Oz$ for every open $O$. Consequently $q|_{uV}:uV\to q(uV)$ is a homeomorphism for each $u$, and transport the translated Hilbert charts through these maps. On an overlap, two lifts differ locally by multiplication by a fixed element of the discrete group $Z_N$, so chart changes are smooth. Distinct cosets have disjoint open neighborhoods: if $v^{-1}w\notin Z_N$, continuity and finiteness give neighborhoods $O_v,O_w$ with $O_v^{-1}O_w\cap Z_N=\varnothing$, and their images under $q$ are disjoint. Thus the quotient is Hausdorff. Its countable base descends from that of the Sobolev section space by the open map $q$. Multiplication and inversion are smooth in these charts because they lift locally to the corresponding smooth operations on $\mathcal G_{k+1}$. This defines a Hilbert Lie group with the stated quotient topology, and $q$ is a local diffeomorphism.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty:=\Gamma^\infty(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ be the group of smooth adjoint-group sections under pointwise multiplication, identified above with the smooth gauge group. Give it the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. For a connection form $\omega$, write $A_\alpha=s_\alpha^*\omega$ for its local form. The right-principal convention gives $A_\beta=g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}A_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}+g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}dg_{\alpha\beta}$. The right gauge action is locally $A_\alpha^u:=u_\alpha^{-1}A_\alpha u_\alpha+u_\alpha^{-1}du_\alpha$. For smooth $u$, this is the pullback by $\widetilde u$: for $X\in T_xM$, $d(\widetilde u\circ s_\alpha)_xX=d(R_{u_\alpha(x)})_{s_\alpha(x)}\,ds_\alpha(X)+(u_\alpha^{-1}du_\alpha(X))_P(s_\alpha(x)u_\alpha(x))$, and the connection equivariance and vertical reproduction identities give the displayed formula. For Sobolev $u$, the calculus lemma verifies that the local forms patch under the stated transition rules and define a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$.
